title: 330. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Congruence by SSS
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the SSS congruence criterion for triangles.
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the SSS congruence criterion for triangles?

options.label: A
options.text: If the three sides of one triangle are respectively equal to the three sides of another triangle, then the two triangles are congruent.

options.label: B
options.text: If two sides and one angle of one triangle are respectively equal to two sides and one angle of another triangle, then the two triangles are congruent.

questions.explanation: SSS stands for Side-Side-Side. The criterion states that when all three pairs of corresponding sides of two triangles are equal, the two triangles are congruent. Option B is not always true because the angle must be the included angle for SAS; otherwise, congruence is not guaranteed.
questions.hint: Recall what each letter in SSS represents.

questions.learningObjective: Apply SSS to identify congruent triangles from given side equalities.
questions.question: In triangles \(ABC\) and \(DEF\), \(AB=DE\), \(BC=EF\), and \(CA=FD\). Which congruence criterion directly matches the given data and proves that the triangles are congruent?
questions.explanation: The given equalities match all three pairs of corresponding sides: \(AB\) with \(DE\), \(BC\) with \(EF\), and \(CA\) with \(FD\). Therefore, the SSS criterion proves \(\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF\). SAS would require two sides and the included angle, which are not given.
questions.hint: Compare the given equalities with the meaning of SSS.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the conclusion from three pairs of equal corresponding sides.
questions.question: In triangles \(ABC\) and \(PQR\), \(AB=PQ\), \(BC=QR\), and \(AC=PR\). What can be concluded?

options.label: A
options.text: The triangles are similar but not necessarily congruent.

options.label: B
options.text: The triangles are congruent by SSS.

questions.explanation: The three pairs of corresponding sides are equal: \(AB=PQ\), \(BC=QR\), and \(AC=PR\). By the SSS criterion, \(\triangle ABC \cong \triangle PQR\). Similarity alone would not require equal side lengths, so option A is weaker than what is guaranteed.
questions.hint: Check whether all three pairs of corresponding sides are known to be equal.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the additional side equality needed for SSS congruence.
questions.question: Triangles \(ABC\) and \(DEF\) have \(AB=DE\) and \(BC=EF\). Which additional equality directly completes the stated data to prove the triangles congruent by SSS?
questions.explanation: SSS requires all three pairs of corresponding sides to be equal. The two given equalities are \(AB=DE\) and \(BC=EF\), so the remaining pair is \(AC\) and \(DF\). The angle equality in A would suggest SAS if it were the included angle, not SSS.
questions.hint: List the three pairs of sides that SSS requires.

questions.learningObjective: Find a missing side length needed for SSS congruence.
questions.question: Triangle \(PQR\) has side lengths \(5\text{ cm}\), \(7\text{ cm}\), and \(9\text{ cm}\). Triangle \(XYZ\) has side lengths \(5\text{ cm}\), \(7\text{ cm}\), and \(x\text{ cm}\). For the triangles to be congruent by SSS, what must \(x\) be?
questions.explanation: For SSS congruence, the three side lengths of the two triangles must match. The first triangle has sides \(5,7,9\), so the missing side in the second triangle must be \(9\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Match the given side lengths of the first triangle with those of the second.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether two triangles are congruent using three pairs of equal sides.
questions.question: Triangles \(MNO\) and \(PQR\) have \(MN=PQ=6\), \(NO=QR=8\), and \(OM=RP=10\). Which statement is true?

options.label: A
options.text: They are not congruent because no angles are given.

questions.explanation: The three pairs of corresponding sides are equal: \(MN=PQ\), \(NO=QR\), and \(OM=RP\). By the SSS criterion, the triangles are congruent. Angles are not needed when all three side pairs are equal.
questions.hint: Apply the SSS criterion directly to the three side equalities.

questions.learningObjective: Identify sufficient information for proving triangles congruent by SSS.
questions.question: Which information is sufficient to prove two triangles congruent by SSS?

options.label: A
options.text: The three side lengths of one triangle are respectively equal to the three side lengths of the other triangle.

options.label: B
options.text: Two side lengths and the included angle of one triangle are respectively equal to those of the other triangle.

questions.explanation: SSS uses only the three pairs of corresponding sides. If all three side lengths match respectively, the triangles are congruent. Option B describes the SAS criterion, not SSS.
questions.hint: Recall which parts of a triangle are used in the SSS criterion.

questions.learningObjective: Apply SSS to overlapping triangles with a common side.
questions.question: In triangles \(ABD\) and \(ACD\), \(AB=AC\), \(BD=CD\), and \(AD\) is common. Which congruence statement directly matches the supplied side equalities?
questions.explanation: The equalities are \(AB=AC\), \(BD=CD\), and \(AD=AD\). These are three pairs of corresponding sides: \(AB\) with \(AC\), \(BD\) with \(CD\), and \(AD\) with itself. Therefore, SSS proves \(\triangle ABD \cong \triangle ACD\).
questions.hint: Identify the three pairs of equal sides, including the common side.

questions.learningObjective: Use SSS congruence to find the perimeter of a triangle.
questions.question: Triangles \(ABC\) and \(DEF\) are congruent by SSS. If \(AB=DE=7\), \(BC=EF=24\), and \(AC=DF=25\), what is the perimeter of triangle \(DEF\)?
questions.explanation: Since the triangles are congruent by SSS, corresponding sides are equal. Triangle \(DEF\) has sides \(DE=7\), \(EF=24\), and \(DF=25\). Its perimeter is \(7+24+25=56\).
questions.hint: Use the corresponding side equalities to find the three side lengths of triangle \(DEF\), then add them.

questions.learningObjective: Solve for an unknown side expression using SSS congruence.
questions.question: Triangles \(ABC\) and \(DEF\) are congruent by SSS. In triangle \(ABC\), \(AB=2x\), \(BC=10\), and \(AC=12\). In triangle \(DEF\), \(DE=8\), \(EF=10\), and \(DF=12\). What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: Since the triangles are congruent by SSS, corresponding sides are equal. Matching \(BC=EF=10\) and \(AC=DF=12\) leaves \(AB=DE\). Thus \(2x=8\), so \(x=4\).
questions.hint: Match the equal corresponding sides first, then solve for \(x\).
